properties.name: Pueblo Bonito
properties.alignment: Back wall aligned to true north within 0.1°; solstice sunrise and sunset mark interior corner rooms
properties.note: Largest great house at Chaco. One of the most studied prehistoric structures in North America. Construction spanned roughly three centuries.

properties.name: Chetro Ketl
properties.note: Features an unusual colonnade — unique in all Chacoan architecture. Contains a great kiva and multiple smaller kivas.
properties.excavated_by: Edgar Hewett, School of American Research, 1920–1940

properties.name: Pueblo del Arroyo
properties.note: Adjoins a rare tri-walled circular structure — only two known at Chaco, purpose unknown. Significantly later construction than the core great houses.

properties.name: Casa Rinconada
properties.alignment: NE doorway aligns to summer solstice sunrise at 66.5°; four equally-spaced roof support niches align to cardinal directions
properties.note: Largest isolated great kiva at Chaco — not attached to a residential great house. Likely a community ceremonial space open to the broader canyon population.

properties.name: Hungo Pavi
properties.note: One of the least excavated great houses in the canyon. Most rooms remain unexcavated. Interior great kiva still largely unexamined.

properties.name: Una Vida
properties.note: One of the earliest great houses. A nearby cliff face bears extensive petroglyph panels. Generally considered among the three founding great houses of the Chacoan system.

properties.name: Penasco Blanco
properties.note: Westernmost great house. Located near a cliff face bearing a pictograph panel that may depict the A.D. 1054 supernova (SN 1054, now the Crab Nebula), the crescent moon, and a handprint.

properties.name: Pueblo Alto
properties.alignment: Situated on canyon rim at terminus of the Great North Road; positioned for inter-site visibility across the road network
properties.note: Mesa-top location with long sight lines in all directions. Junction point for multiple Chacoan roads. Trash mounds suggest periodic large gatherings.

properties.name: Kin Kletso
properties.note: Later construction than the core great houses, likely representing the McElmo Black-on-white architectural tradition. More compact and regularly planned than earlier structures.

properties.name: Wijiji
properties.note: Easternmost great house. Unusually symmetrical and compact for its size. Reached via a 3-mile round-trip canyon trail past extensive petroglyph panels.
